scope: Host mechanism observations only, not TTFT acceptance or causal proof
hypothesis: Steady prefill layer-interval differences may accompany increased host CPU work or runnable-thread delay; these measurements distinguish those observables, not GPU busy vs CUDA polling spin.
instrumentation: Q4T_LAYER_TIMING=1 and host_interval_probe.so, no CUDA launch interception or Nsight
analyzed_chunks: 2..25 only; chunk1 establishes counters after initialization
validity: Guard exits COMPLETED, no HTTP output/capacity failure
Exactly 25 host reports with seq 0..24 on one TID and matching 24x8192+8181 layer records
pmu_error=0, sched_error=0, usage_rc=0, all counters monotonic
Every analyzed interval has PMU running/enabled >=0.99; otherwise mark PMU comparison invalid without rerun
Every capture after initialization <=1ms, total captures <=5ms; this bounds capture only, not log writing or initialization effects
report: Sum and per-chunk wall, thread CPU, runqueue, switches, user-only PMU counts, layer-event interval
For each metric same-identity R=max(abs(A2-A1),abs(B2-B1)) and both paired B-A deltas
A version-associated observable requires both paired deltas positive and > its R; no significance or causal assertion
If event differences resolve but host observables do not, move to device/driver dependency observation; do not label residual GPU busy
If host observable resolves, require attribution of CPU execution vs CUDA spin before claiming host cause
limitations: Instrumentation TTFT never used as performance acceptance
First chunk excluded, first PMU init can cost tens of milliseconds
Thread CPU includes kernel; PMU excludes kernel/hypervisor
CPU time can include spin while waiting for GPU; not equivalent to submission work
No schedstat zero-value proof of absent global contention
Aggregate observation alone cannot establish causality
stop_rules: Any phase/HTTP error stops; retain original evidence and never auto-retry
No extra warmups, probes, samples or post-hoc gate changes
